conceptual assets.information: The per-channel enable setting determines whether PWM activity is enabled and whether the channel requests its clock. It enters with channel configuration writes and leaves through configuration read-back and the clock-enable output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality no: this is an operational enable setting, not information the RTL indicates is secret. Integrity yes: an asserted channel write loads cfg_en from wdata_i at lines 183-184, with no restricting check. Availability yes: cfg_en drives clkgen_en_o at line 197 and disables or clears PWM progression at lines 212-225, so changing it can disable the channel. Undermined Expected Behavior no: the RTL contains no privileged-mode, override, bypass or test behavior acting on this setting.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue a channel write with cfg_en cleared, disabling the PWM channel and its clock request.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel prescaler selection and clock-divider limit determine the rate at which PWM duty progression advances. The settings enter through channel configuration writes and are returned through configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality no: the timing settings are operational configuration rather than secret information. Integrity yes: channel writes load cfg_prsc and cfg_cdiv at lines 183, 185 and 187, and these values control clock selection, divider comparison and tick generation at lines 214-220. Availability yes: the selected clkgen_i bit and divider determine whether cnt_tick is produced at lines 214-217, so a modified setting can withhold PWM progression. Undermined Expected Behavior no: no privileged, override, bypass or test behavior is present.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite the prescaler or divider so that PWM ticks occur at an incorrect rate or do not occur.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel polarity and duty settings determine the output level and duty cycle of the PWM waveform. They enter through configuration writes, are returned through read-back, and the polarity value also contributes to the PWM output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality no: polarity and duty are externally observable operational settings, not information the RTL indicates is secret. Integrity yes: channel writes load cfg_pol and cfg_duty at lines 183, 186 and 188, and those settings determine pwm_o at lines 231-234. Availability no: changing polarity or duty changes waveform behavior but does not by itself block the PWM engine or withhold a required transfer. Undermined Expected Behavior no: the RTL has no integration-level privileged, override, bypass or test path acting on these settings.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite the polarity or duty fields so the PWM output has an incorrect waveform.

conceptual assets.information: The decoded channel selection determines which generated PWM channel receives or returns a bus access. It has no boundary crossing of its own because it only decides which child write and read strobes are asserted.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality no: the selection is an access-routing decision, not secret information. Integrity yes: bus_req_i.addr selects a channel at line 109 and the resulting sel controls the write and read strobes at lines 110-111, so a changed selection can target the wrong channel. Availability yes: an address that selects no generated channel leaves the access strobes inactive at lines 109-111, causing the requested channel transfer to be lost. Undermined Expected Behavior no: no privileged, override, bypass or test behavior acts on the selection.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the access address to redirect a configuration or read operation to another channel or to no channel.

conceptual assets.information: The generated PWM waveform is the timing and level behavior delivered to the external consumer on pwm_o. It is produced internally from the channel enable, timing, duty and polarity state and has no entering port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality no: pwm_o is an intended external output and the RTL provides no indication that its waveform is secret. Integrity yes: pwm_o is selected from cfg_pol according to cfg_en, cnt_duty and cfg_duty at lines 231-234, so modifying channel configuration changes the produced waveform. Availability yes: cfg_en can clear the PWM progression and force non-progressing output behavior at lines 212-225 and 231-234, allowing the PWM function to be disabled. Undermined Expected Behavior no: the RTL contains no privileged-mode, override, bypass or test behavior acting on the waveform.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could rewrite a channel configuration to force an incorrect or effectively disabled waveform on pwm_o.

considered, not kept.reason: The selected clkgen_i bit only advances the divider and cnt_cdiv, cnt_tick and cnt_duty only pace PWM steps at lines 214-227, so the pacing-pulse and sequencing-state rules bar them as separate information.
The request strobe and read/write fields only control whether channel accesses occur at lines 69 and 110-111, so they are access command fields rather than a separate conceptual asset.
bus_rsp_o.ack repeats the request strobe and bus_rsp_o.err is tied to a constant at lines 69-76, so the bus-handshake-copy and constant-status rules bar a separate concept.
rdata and rdata_sum only carry or merge channel configuration read-back through lines 86-88 and 102, so they add no information beyond the configuration concepts.
